children: Canadian mobile carriers might have another player to contend with on the national stage as Globalive founder Anthony Lacavera plans to launch a standalone wireless operator in Canada. The move comes amid debate over whether Quebecor's C$31 billion bid for Telus would shrink the sector from four major competitors back to three. Using Bermuda-based Paradise Mobile's 5G technology, Lacavera is pitching Globalive as a fourth-carrier option in a sector dominated by a handful of communication and media conglomerates. "Any consolidation the government approves must make room for an independent, pure-play wireless carrier," Lacavera says, noting a wireless-only rival can undercut prices without cannibalizing legacy cable or TV bundles. Still, Globalive could face an uphill regulatory battle after Prime Minister Mark Carney suggested earlier this month that fewer players can sometimes still foster competition.
